help.ai.box:
Precautions:
  • AIs can be wrong — their answer is an opinion, not a truth.
  • Never paste a password, key or personal data.
  • The final decision (allow, block, delete) is yours.
help.ai.intro: The inspection cards and the blocked domains table offer a “Copy for an AI” button. It prepares a complete text (context + data + question) that you can paste as-is into ChatGPT, Mistral, Claude or any other assistant.
help.ai.li1: Per item — the 🤖 icon on each row (alerts, blocked domains, parental and home logs) copies the info for that item only; the button shows a green “✓” to confirm.
help.ai.li2: Global — the “🤖 Analyze all” button above each log exports the complete list of blocks (up to 100 entries) for an overall analysis.
help.ai.title: Ask an AI for an opinion
help.broken.box: A blocked domain is not proof of danger: the lists also block telemetry and some legitimate CDNs. Known infrastructure domains (Google, Microsoft, GitHub…) are allowed automatically.
help.broken.intro: If a service stopped responding while filtering is active, a domain it depends on was probably blocked:
help.broken.li2: Find the domain in “Top blocked domains” or in the detail table.
help.broken.li3: Click “Allow” — the domain is unblocked immediately, no restart.
help.broken.li4: If you change your mind: the button becomes “Re-block” — one click removes the allowance and the domain becomes blockable again.
help.broken.title: A website or app stopped working
help.faq.q1:
“28 blocked domains but only 5 in the list?”
The counter totals blocked requests; the same domain can account for several requests.
help.faq.q2:
“Is a blocked domain a virus?”
No. DNS blocking is a comfort/privacy measure, not malware detection.
help.faq.q3:
“Does allowing a domain make my PC vulnerable?”
It only lifts the DNS block for that domain. The rest of the filtering and the firewall stay active.
help.faq.q4:
“Why notifications at first startup?”
The grace period (~60 s) now suppresses them; what remains corresponds to real recent blocks.
help.faq.q5:
“I forgot / I don't have a Windows password?”
By default the app uses a dedicated password (“app” method): it is created at first launch and works even on passwordless Windows Hello accounts. The “Windows session” method in Settings requires a Windows account with a password. To disable the lock: access.enabled: false in web_port_dashboard/config.yml.
help.faq.title: Frequently asked questions
help.filter.act1: Allow adds the domain to the whitelist (immediate effect); Re-block cancels the allowance.
help.filter.act2: Reset DNS restores the default whitelist: all manual allowances and disabling are erased.
help.filter.act3: The 🔎 and 🤖 buttons on each row open the detail card or copy the info for an AI; “🤖 Analyze all” exports the whole list in one click.
help.filter.li1: The filter intercepts DNS queries from the whole PC.
help.filter.li2: A domain present in the EasyList/EasyPrivacy lists receives the 0.0.0.0 response — it becomes unreachable.
help.filter.li3: The whitelist takes precedence: an allowed domain is never blocked, even if it appears in a list.
help.filter.li4: “via …” in the table means the block comes from the parent domain (e.g. ads.example.com blocked via the rule on example.com).
help.filter.li5: At startup, a grace period (~60 s) suppresses notifications to avoid a burst of alerts.
help.filter.title: How filtering works
help.glossary.dga.def: Automatically generated domain (random string of letters) — typical of malware.
help.glossary.dns.def: Service that translates a domain name into an IP address. Filtering operates at this level.
help.glossary.fw.def: The Windows firewall filters inbound/outbound connections by rules.
help.glossary.listening.def: The program is waiting for incoming connections on this port.
help.glossary.loopback.def: Loopback: accessible only from this PC — much less risky.
help.glossary.pid.def: Numeric identifier of the Windows process.
help.glossary.port.def: Numeric “door” through which a program communicates over the network (e.g. 443 for HTTPS).
help.glossary.sha.def: Unique fingerprint of a file — allows a program to be identified with certainty.
help.glossary.title: Glossary
help.glossary.tracker.def: Service that collects usage data (statistics, advertising). Blocking a tracker can break a feature.
help.glossary.whitelist.def: White list: explicitly allowed domains or IPs, taking precedence over blocks.
help.glossary.zero.def: The port listens on all interfaces → exposed to the entire local network (and potentially the Internet).
help.liability.box:
Cerbere Security Shield provides information, diagnostic tools and recommendations.
                    Decisions made on their basis — allowing a domain, banning an IP, closing a port,
                    consulting an external AI — are the user's responsibility.
                    The displayed risk levels are automatic indications: they constitute
                    neither a guarantee of safety nor proof of danger.
help.liability.li1: DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH): a browser can bypass the local DNS. The “doh_bypass” category blocks known public resolvers, but it is recommended to disable DoH in the child's browsers.
help.liability.li2: VPN: an active VPN bypasses filtering. The “vpn” category blocks known providers' sites, not an already installed VPN client.
help.liability.li3: Administrator account: an admin user can stop the backend. For real protection, the child's session must be a non-administrator account.
help.liability.li4: Quota: measured by DNS activity (minutes with queries), not exact screen time.
help.liability.li5: Binary blocking: a domain is blocked entirely — impossible to “browse without paying” on the same domain.
help.liability.li6: Cookies: one-off audit (closed browsers recommended), no real-time filtering — encrypted HTTPS does not allow interception.
help.liability.lock: Password locking protects the interface against unauthorized use in front of the screen. It does not protect against a user who already has full technical access to the machine.
help.liability.pc_box: Blocking relies on the local DNS: it is effective but not foolproof.
help.liability.title: Limits & responsibility
help.links.grc: External test: probes your machine from the Internet and reveals the ports that are really exposed — the only test seen from outside.

help.links.sans: Port sheet + global attack statistics — “is this port a frequent target?”.

help.links.title: External resources — what the links are for
help.links.vt: Analyzes a hash or file name with ~70 antivirus engines. The most comprehensive for “is this file malware?”.

help.parental.box: After a block is enabled, the browser may still display an already-open site (DNS cache + existing connections). Close and reopen the browser for a reliable test — see the “Limits & responsibility” section.
help.parental.intro: Two modules complement tracker filtering, both protected by a PIN code (4–8 digits) separate from the application password:
help.parental.kp1: The PIN opens a 10-minute session: creating, editing or deleting rules, enabling/disabling and stopping the application require the PIN as long as protection is active.
help.parental.kp2: The blocking log of each tab lists intercepted domains with the triggered rule; 🔎 opens the card, 🤖 copies for an AI, “Analyze all” exports the whole log.
help.parental.kp3: Reset (under PIN) erases all module rules and disables protection.
help.parental.kp4: The Home control tab also offers a cookie audit (Chrome, Edge, Firefox): flags cookies linked to sensitive domains and allows targeted purging.
help.parental.kp5: Quitting Cerbere from the notification icon requires the PIN if protection is active; without the PIN, the icon closes but filtering continues in the background.
help.parental.li1: Parental control — blocks entire categories (adult, gambling, drugs, scams, malware, social networks…) or specific domains. Three modes per rule: permanently blocked, time window (e.g. allowed 6 PM–8 PM), daily quota (e.g. 30 min of activity).
help.parental.li2: Home control — blocks domains sensitive for the household: payments and banks, online shopping, public DoH resolvers (which would bypass filtering) and VPN sites.
help.parental.title: Parental & home control
help.plans.box: A plan modifies Windows firewall rules. Check the list of targeted ports before applying.
help.plans.li1: Check the ports to handle in the Active Ports tab.
help.plans.li2: Generate a hardening plan (protect) or a release plan (unblock).
help.plans.li3: Apply from the Cerbere icon: right-click in the notification area → “Apply hardening plan” or “Apply release plan”.
help.plans.li4: A Windows notification confirms the success or failure of the application.
help.plans.title: The security plan cycle
help.port.box: Still unsure? Use the “Copy for an AI” button in the process card: it prepares a complete text to paste into ChatGPT or another assistant.
help.port.li1: In the Active Ports tab, click the port row (or “Inspect”).
help.port.li2: Read the card: process name, executable path, command line.
help.port.li3: Look at the SHA-256 hash and click “Check reputation”: Cerbere queries MalwareBazaar (database of known malware).
help.port.li4: If needed, the external links open a search on VirusTotal, ProcessLibrary, SpeedGuide or SANS ISC.
help.port.li5: If the process is unknown to you and worrying: check the port and generate a hardening plan (see dedicated section).
help.port.title: A port looks suspicious — what to do?
help.risk.box: A high risk level does not mean your PC is infected — it flags an exposure that deserves checking.
help.risk.critical: Sensitive port exposed (database, file sharing, remote administration). Action: check the process, consider a hardening plan.
help.risk.intro: Each open port receives an automatic assessment:
help.risk.protected: Port already covered by a Windows firewall rule. No action needed.
help.risk.title: Understanding risk levels
help.risk.unexpected: Open port matching no expected service. Action: inspect the associated process.
help.risk.vulnerable: Port exposed to the network AND not protected by the firewall. This is the priority.
help.welcome.box: If in doubt about a displayed item, see the “Ask an AI for an opinion” section — it lets you export the information in one click for analysis.
help.welcome.intro: Cerbere continuously monitors your machine from three angles:
help.welcome.li1: Active ports — which programs listen on the network, and what risk level they represent;
help.welcome.li2: Intrusion detection — suspicious inbound connections and port scans, with automatic banning;
help.welcome.li3: Filtering & trackers — DNS blocking of advertising and telemetry domains (EasyList/EasyPrivacy lists).
help.welcome.nav: Use the tabs at the top to navigate. Hover over any button or heading for a moment: a tooltip explains its role.
help.welcome.title: Welcome to Cerbere Security Shield

Exposed sensitive ports: databases, file sharing,
remote administration, etc. Handle first.
ports.filter.fw.title:
Ports already protected by a Windows firewall rule.
No action needed.
ports.filter.label: Risk:
ports.filter.unexpected.title:
Open ports matching no expected or known service.
Potentially suspicious — check the associated process.
ports.filter.vulnerable.title:
Ports both exposed to the network AND not protected by the firewall.
This is the most at-risk category.
ports.row.title: Click to inspect process details
ports.search.clear.title: Clear search
ports.search.title:
Filters the table live as you type:
process name, port number, protocol, IP address or PID.
ports.th.action.title:
“Inspect” opens the detailed process card:
executable path, SHA-256 hash, MalwareBazaar reputation,
and external links (VirusTotal, SpeedGuide, SANS…).
ports.th.ip.title:
Local IP address the port listens on.
0.0.0.0 or :: = all interfaces → exposed to the entire network.
127.0.0.1 = loopback → accessible only from this PC.
ports.th.pid.title: Identifier of the Windows process that owns this port.
ports.th.port.title: Number of the listening network port.
ports.th.process.title: Name of the program associated with the port.
ports.th.protocol.title: TCP or UDP.
ports.th.risk.title:
Automatically assessed level:
critical (sensitive) / unexpected (unknown) / protected (firewall) / vulnerable (exposed unprotected).
ports.th.select_all.title: Checks or unchecks all visible ports in the table.
ports.th.state.title: LISTENING = the service is waiting for incoming connections.
settings.access.app_password.hint: Sets or replaces the dedicated password (stored as a hash, never in plain text).
settings.access.lock_now.title:
Locks the application immediately:
the unlock screen will be shown.
settings.access.title: Access security
settings.btn.save.title:
Saves all settings to config.yml.
Settings with immediate effect are applied without restart.
settings.classif.hint: Comma-separated lists. Used by the risk assessment.
settings.classif.title: Port classification
settings.ext.enabled: Send critical alerts to an external channel
settings.ext.hint: Webhook is recommended: simpler and more reliable than SMTP. Use an “app password” for Gmail.
settings.ext.title: External alerts (email / webhook)
settings.filter.grace.hint: Duration without Windows notifications when the filter starts (default: 60 s).
settings.filter.title: Filtering & Trackers
settings.language.hint: Applied to the interface immediately and kept on next launch.
settings.language.label: Interface language:
settings.language.title: Language
settings.lists.auto_update.hint: At launch, stale lists are re-downloaded in the background (never blocking), then checked every 24 h.
settings.lists.th.domains.title: Number of domains available in this list.
settings.lists.th.family.title: Family: ad blocker or parental/home category.
settings.lists.th.list.title: Name of the list or category.
settings.lists.th.status.title:
OK = list up to date · stale = old cache kept ·
missing = never downloaded · error = unreadable cache.
settings.lists.title: Blocking lists
settings.lists.update_all.title:
Re-downloads ALL lists: ad blocker
(EasyList, AdGuard, OISD, HaGeZi…) and enabled
parental/home categories.

If the network fails, the existing cache is kept.
settings.scan.hint: Port scan frequency (default: 30 s). Applied on the next cycle, without restart.
settings.scan.title: Network scan
status.audit_done: Audit recommendations applied ({count} unprotected port(s) included).
status.config_save_error: Error saving the configuration on the server (local cache updated).
status.config_saved: Current configuration saved on the server.
status.harden_error: Error while generating the hardening plan
status.no_ports_harden: No ports selected for the hardening plan.
status.no_ports_release: No ports selected for the release plan.
status.no_ports_save: No ports to save in the configuration.
status.no_ports_suggested: No ports detected to apply a suggested configuration.
status.release_error: Error while generating the release plan
status.suggested_applied: Suggested configuration applied based on critical/unexpected ports.
tabs.adblock.title:
Multi-list ad blocker: EasyList, EasyPrivacy,
AdGuard, OISD, HaGeZi — individually checkable.

Enabled lists are merged and applied to DNS filtering
for all applications on the PC (immediate effect).
tabs.alerts.title:
Log of suspicious events: new ports, unknown processes, network anomalies.

Each alert can be inspected (path, SHA-256 hash, reputation) or deleted.
tabs.domestic.title:
Home control: online payment lock, blocking of
VPN/proxies and DNS bypass, browser cookie hygiene.

Protected by the parental PIN code.
tabs.filter.title:
DNS blocking of trackers and ads (EasyList/EasyPrivacy lists).

Known legitimate services are whitelisted automatically.
You can allow or block domains manually.
tabs.help.title:
Help and documentation: glossary, common scenarios,
usage guide for plans and filtering.
tabs.history.title:
Periodic captures of the network state.

Allows comparing the evolution of open ports over time.
tabs.intrusion.title:
Continuous network monitoring: inbound connections, port scans and banned IPs.

Monitoring starts automatically with the application.
tabs.parental.title:
Parental control: category filtering (adult, gambling,
social networks…), time windows and daily quotas.

Settings are protected by a PIN code (10-minute session).
tabs.ports.title:
Real-time view of open ports on this machine.

Check ports then generate a hardening or release plan.
Click a table row to inspect the associated process.
tabs.settings.title:
Application settings: scan interval,
notifications, account and email alerts.
